articles.title: Introverts experience greater mood elevations from antidepressant placebos than extraverts
articles.summary: A new study indicates that introverts and individuals with lower natural joy experience the greatest mood boosts from dopamine-altering drugs and antidepressant placebos. The findings suggest that baseline personality heavily influences how people respond to mood treatments.

articles.summary: arXiv:2608.06417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The proliferation of misinformation online has driven demand for scalable detection systems. articles.summary: arXiv:2608.06427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models can reproduce an observational distribution while encoding an incorrect causal structure. articles.title: Fear of missing out on AI is linked to anxiety and depression
articles.summary: A new study finds that as artificial intelligence advances, the fear of falling behind is creating a measurable psychological burden. Fortunately, building practical competence with these new digital tools can help protect your mental health.

articles.title: Scientists discover a previously unknown cognitive benefit of aerobic exercise
articles.summary: Scientists have found that a brief session of moderate cycling protects the brain's automatic recalibration process. The study highlights how acute exercise helps the nervous system maintain its ability to adjust movements without conscious effort.

articles.title: Frequent cannabis users wake up with their “stress hormone” already elevated
articles.summary: Frequent cannabis users may wake up with unusually high levels of the stress hormone cortisol, suggesting their daily stress rhythms could be disrupted. Researchers say the finding raises questions about whether using cannabis for stress relief might, over time, interfere with the very system that helps the body handle stress.

articles.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
articles.summary: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat triggered striking changes across the brain and body, including shifts tied to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and natural pain relief. Participants also showed brain connectivity patterns resembling those associated with psychedelic experiences, suggesting that powerful altered states may be achievable without drugs.
